043/**
044 * Provides String based properties like {@link System#getProperty(String)} for default
045 * configuration of logging levels and output. Since Rainbow Gum is configuration agnostic
046 * LogProperties is a simple string key and string value interface to allow almost any
047 * configuration implementation. The only required method to implement is
048 * {@link #valueOrNull(String)} and thus LogProperties is a functional like interface but
049 * using {@link LogProperties#builder()} is preferred so that a
050 * {@linkplain #description(String) description} can be added.
051 * <p>
052 * If a custom {@link LogProperties} is not configured the default RainbowGum uses System
053 * properties.
054 * <p>
055 * The built-in properties to configure RainbowGum are modeled after <a href=
056 * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/3.1.0/reference/html/features.html#features.logging">
057 * Spring Boot logging </a>
058 * <p>
059 * LogProperties should generally be accessed with {@link #forKey(String)} (see
060 * {@link LogProperty}) which will allow safe <em>programmatic</em> data conversion of the
061 * flat key values and useful error messages to users if the property cannot be mapped or
062 * is missing. For more <em>declarative</em> injection of properties see
063 * {@link LogConfigurable} which will generate builders that can use LogProperties.
064 * <p>
065 * Rainbow Gum treats {@value #SEP} in the keys as special separator analogous to
066 * JavaScript/JSON and various other configuration systems. Furthermore to work with a
067 * wide set of configuration systems once a property key has a value it is
068 * <strong>RECOMMENDED</strong> that there should not be other property key value with a
069 * key that is a prefix of the previously mentioned key. For example allowing two
070 * properties <code>logging.example=stuff</code>, <code>logging.example.a=A</code> is not
071 * recommended as <code>logging.example</code> is defined as a leaf. The exception to this
072 * rule is keys that end with a logger name, such as levels, for consistency with Spring
073 * Boot. {@link AbstractNested} is one way for a nested format to read them.
074 * <p>
075 * Rainbow Gum out of the the box supports parsing two formats into properties:
076 * {@link Properties} text, and {@link URI#getRawQuery()} percent encoded query
077 * parameters. The two different formats have different behavior for
078 * {@link #listOrNull(String)} and {@link #mapOrNull(String)}. If a custom format of
079 * LogProperties is created those two methods may need to be extended.
080 * <p>
081 * A convention used through out Rainbow Gum is to have the property names as constants as
082 * it makes documentation easier. These constants name are suffixed with
083 * <code>_PROPERTY</code> or <code>_PREFIX</code> the former being a fully qualified key
084 * that maybe parameterized and the latter being a partial key ending with
085 * "<code>.</code>". The fully qualified keys are like leaves on a tree.
086 * <p>
087 * Property keys can be parameterized by using
088 * {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Map)} and a general pattern is
089 * <code>logging.component.{name}.prop</code> where {@value #NAME} is a parameter. Many
090 * property constants use this to allow multiple configuration of components by name.
091 *
092 * <table class="table">
093 * <caption><strong>Built-in Property Patterns</strong></caption>
094 * <tr>
095 * <th>Property Pattern</th>
096 * <th>Description</th>
097 * </tr>
098 * <tr>
099 * <td>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = LEVEL</td>
100 * <td>Sets the level for the logger. If logger name is missing or is <code>root</code>
101 * then it is considered the root logger. {@link Level#INFO} is the default level for the
102 * root logger.</td>
103 * </tr>
104 * <tr>
105 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} = {@link ChangeMode}</td>
106 * <td>Whether runtime changes are on for the configuration. Default is
107 * {@link ChangeMode#OFF}. When on, the loggers that may change are chosen with
108 * {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX}.</td>
109 * </tr>
110 * <tr>
111 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = boolean |
112 * List&lt;{@link ChangeType}&gt;</td>
113 * <td>What may change at runtime for the logger and its children. By design RainbowGum
114 * does not allow loggers to change levels once initialized. Default is none. Has no
115 * effect unless {@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} is on.</td>
116 * </tr>
117 * <tr>
118 * <td>{@value #ROUTES_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
119 * <td>A comma separated list of routes that should be enabled. If not set
120 * {@value LogRouter.Router#DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME } is the default.</td>
121 * </tr>
122 * <tr>
123 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
124 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders associated with the route. If not set
125 * {@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} is used.</td>
126 * </tr>
127 * <tr>
128 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
129 * <td>A comma separated list of {@linkplain LogRouter.Router.Filter filters} applied in
130 * order to the route's events. Default is none.</td>
131 * </tr>
132 * <tr>
133 * <td>{@value #FILTER_PREFIX} + <code>propertyName</code></td>
134 * <td>Configures a filter listed in {@value #ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY}, where
135 * <code>filter</code> is the name it is listed with, for example
136 * <code>logging.route.default.filter.throttle.rate</code>.</td>
137 * </tr>
138 * <tr>
139 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY} = <code>URI</code></td>
140 * <td>Looks up a publisher by URI scheme using the {@link LogPublisherRegistry}. The
141 * publisher is then configured by the other properties starting with
142 * {@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX}.</td>
143 * </tr>
144 * <tr>
145 * <td>{@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
146 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
147 * <td>Configures the route's publisher of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
148 * example <code>logging.route.default.publisher.async.bufferSize</code>. The scheme is
149 * the one written in the URI, so <code>async</code> settings apply to whichever publisher
150 * is registered as <code>async</code>.</td>
151 * </tr>
152 * <tr>
153 * <td>{@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
154 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders that should be enabled. If not set
155 * {@value LogAppender#CONSOLE_APPENDER_NAME} is the default.</td>
156 * </tr>
157 * <tr>
158 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
159 * <td>Looks up an output by URI scheme using the {@link LogOutputRegistry}. The output is
160 * then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX}.</td>
161 * </tr>
162 * <tr>
163 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
164 * <td>Looks up an encoder by URI scheme using the {@link LogEncoderRegistry}. The encoder
165 * is then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #ENCODER_PREFIX}.</td>
166 * </tr>
167 * <tr>
168 * <td>{@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
169 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
170 * <td>Configures the appender's output of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
171 * example <code>logging.appender.file.output.file.bufferSize</code>. An output built
172 * without an appender uses its own name in place of the appender's.</td>
173 * </tr>
174 * <tr>
175 * <td>{@value #ENCODER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
176 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
177 * <td>Configures the appender's encoder of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
178 * example <code>logging.appender.console.encoder.json5.keyValues</code>. Each type has
179 * its own keys, so switching an appender's encoder leaves the other type's settings
180 * unread rather than misread. An encoder built without an appender uses its own name in
181 * place of the appender's.</td>
182 * </tr>
183 * <tr>
184 * <td>{@value #FILE_PROPERTY} = URI</td>
185 * <td>A URI or file path to log to a file. This is for Spring Boot compatibility.</td>
186 * </tr>
187 * </table>
188 *
189 * @see LogConfigurable
190 */
191public interface LogProperties {
192
193        /**
194         * properties separator.
195         */
196        static final String SEP = ".";
197
198        /**
199         * Logging properties prefix.
200         */
201        static final String ROOT_PREFIX = "logging" + SEP;
202
203        /**
204         * Controls direct fail-safe bootstrap diagnostics. {@code OFF} (also {@code false})
205         * is the default; {@code ERROR} dumps on build failure, while {@code INFO} also dumps
206         * after successful config builds. {@code ALL} (also {@code true}) additionally prints
207         * a {@link LogReporter} report after {@link RainbowGum#start()} starts the logging
208         * components. Read from system properties before properties providers run, so it
209         * remains available when loading configuration fails. The system property overrides
210         * {@link LogConfig.Builder#debug(LogConfig.DebugModeType)}.
211         * <p>
212         * Property: <code>{@index logging.debug}</code>
213         */
214        static final String DEBUG_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "debug";
215
216        /**
217         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
218         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
219         * <p>
220         * Property: <code>{@index logging.level.{logger}}</code>
221         */
222        static final String LEVEL_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "level";
223
224        /**
225         * Enabled level groups. The value should be a list of group names used on
226         * {@link #GROUP_PROPERTY}. This is to enable <a href=
227         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
228         * Spring Boot like Log Groups </a>. <em>Note that unlike Spring Boot groups are not
229         * enabled unless this property contains the group.</em>
230         * <p>
231         * Property: <code>{@index logging.groups}</code>
232         */
233        static final String GROUPS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "groups";
234
235        /**
236         * Group property with list of logger names. The level of the group is set with
237         * <code>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code> or on the router itself with
238         * <code>{@value #ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code>. The group name can
239         * also be used in place of a logger name with {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and
240         * {@value #CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX}. This is largely compatible with <a href=
241         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
242         * Spring Boot Log Groups </a>.
243         * <p>
244         * Property: <code>{@index logging.group.{name}}</code>
245         * @see LevelResolver#parseLevel(String)
246         */
247        static final String GROUP_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "group.{name}";
248
249        /**
250         * Whether runtime changes are on: see {@link ChangeMode}.
251         * <p>
252         * Property: <code>{@index logging.change.mode}</code>
253         */
254        static final String CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.mode";
255
256        /**
257         * The level threshold of events captured before Rainbow Gum is fully bound. Before
258         * Rainbow Gum is bound events are queued. By default events that are below
259         * <code>INFO</code> are not queued.
260         * <p>
261         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.queue.level}</code>
262         */
263        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_LEVEL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.level";
264
265        /**
266         * The level threshold of queued events reported to standard error before Rainbow Gum
267         * is bound. Defaults to <code>ERROR</code>.
268         * <p>
269         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.queue.error}</code>
270         */
271        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_ERROR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.error";
272
273        /**
274         * The most events queued while no Rainbow Gum is bound, before one is bound or after
275         * one is closed. Events past it are dropped and counted, and the count is reported as
276         * a warning alert when the next Rainbow Gum is bound. Defaults to <code>1000</code>.
277         * <p>
278         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.queue.size}</code>
279         */
280        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_SIZE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.size";
281
282        /**
283         * Whether starting the global Rainbow Gum registers a JVM shutdown hook that closes
284         * it: <code>on</code> (the default) or <code>off</code>, with <code>true</code> and
285         * <code>false</code> as aliases. Set it to <code>off</code> when the application or
286         * framework closes Rainbow Gum itself as the last step of its own shutdown: JVM
287         * shutdown hooks run concurrently in no set order, so events logged by other hooks
288         * after this one has run are lost, except errors, which are echoed to standard error.
289         * In code, see
290         * {@link LogConfig.Builder#shutdownHook(LogConfig.Globals.ShutdownHookMode)}.
291         * <p>
292         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.shutdownHook}</code>
293         */
294        static final String GLOBAL_SHUTDOWN_HOOK_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.shutdownHook";
295
296        /**
297         * The line separator formatters end lines and stack trace lines with: <code>lf</code>
298         * (default) for <code>\n</code>, <code>crlf</code> for <code>\r\n</code>, or
299         * <code>platform</code> for {@link System#lineSeparator()}. Read once, from system
300         * properties only.
301         * <p>
302         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.lineSeparator}</code>
303         */
304        static final String GLOBAL_LINE_SEPARATOR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.lineSeparator";
305
306        /**
307         * Whether output uses ANSI escape codes: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode}.
308         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode#AUTO}.
309         * <p>
310         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.ansi.mode}</code>
311         */
312        static final String GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.ansi.mode";
313
314        /**
315         * Which kind of lock appenders use: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock}.
316         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock#AUTO}.
317         * <p>
318         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.appender.lock}</code>
319         */
320        static final String GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.appender.lock";
321
322        /**
323         * Whether the logging path may use a {@link ThreadLocal}: see
324         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode}. Default is
325         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode#ALLOW}.
326         * <p>
327         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.threadLocal}</code>
328         */
329        static final String GLOBAL_THREAD_LOCAL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.threadLocal";
330
331        /**
332         * Opts every appender/encoder that has not been given an explicit choice into
333         * whatever this release currently believes is the best buffering/locking strategy for
334         * the platform the process is actually running on, instead of the fixed defaults
335         * ({@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}, a
336         * {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based encode) used otherwise. An explicit
337         * choice - programmatic ({@code appenderType(...)}, {@code useGetBytes(...)}) or via
338         * a more specific property ({@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY}) - always wins
339         * over this property; it only ever fills in what would otherwise be unset.
340         * <p>
341         * <strong>What "best" resolves to today, and why that is not a contract:</strong>
342         * currently this only has an effect under GraalVM native-image (detected the same way
343         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#AUTO_DETECT} is - see its javadoc), where it sets
344         * the default appender type to {@code AUTO_DETECT} (this benchmark's own measurements
345         * found {@code SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} a real, repeatable win over the
346         * plain-JVM default there) and defaults text encoders to
347         * {@code String.getBytes(Charset)}-based encoding over the default
348         * {@code CharsetEncoder}-based one. On a plain JVM this property currently changes
349         * nothing at all - the measurements that motivated the native-image behavior above
350         * pointed the other way on HotSpot. None of this is a promise: as this project
351         * benchmarks more platforms, JDK versions, and encode strategies, what "optimize"
352         * resolves to on a given platform - including whether it does anything on a plain JVM
353         * at all - can and will change between releases without notice. Pin an explicit
354         * appender type/encoder strategy instead if a deployment needs a specific one to
355         * always be used.
356         * <p>
357         * Property: <code>{@index logging.global.optimize}</code>
358         */
359        static final String GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.optimize";
360
361        /**
362         * How the java.util.logging, System.Logger and JBoss Logging message style formats a
363         * message with arguments, named after the implementation that formats the same way:
364         * <ul>
365         * <li><code>jdk</code> (default, alias <code>jboss</code>):
366         * {@link java.text.MessageFormat} is used only when the message has an argument index
367         * such as <code>{0}</code>, so <code>It's done</code> is logged as is. A
368         * {@link Throwable} argument is formatted like any other argument.</li>
369         * <li><code>log4j2</code> (alias <code>logback</code>):
370         * {@link java.text.MessageFormat} is used whenever the message has arguments, so
371         * <code>It's done</code> with an argument is logged as <code>Its done</code>, because
372         * an apostrophe is a quote. A {@link Throwable} that is the last argument is
373         * formatted like any other argument and also logged with its stack trace.</li>
374         * </ul>
375         * <p>
376         * Property: <code>{@index logging.messageformat.style}</code>
377         * @see LogMessageFormatter#ofJUL(LogProperties)
378         */
379        static final String MESSAGE_FORMAT_STYLE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "messageformat.style";
380
381        /**
382         * Key values namespace, for properties that configure where an event's key values
383         * come from.
384         */
385        static final String KEY_VALUES_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "keyvalues" + SEP;
386
387        /**
388         * A comma separated list of the key value sources whose contributors add key values
389         * to events, as the lowercase names of
390         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard}, for example
391         * <code>defaults,slf4j</code>. When absent every source is selected, and an empty
392         * value selects none. A logging facade's own context store is always used for events
393         * logged through that facade, whether or not it is selected, and
394         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor#clear()} clears a store that is not
395         * selected according to
396         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard#clearWhenUnselected()}.
397         * <p>
398         * Property: <code>{@index logging.keyvalues.sources}</code>
399         */
400        static final String KEY_VALUES_SOURCES_PROPERTY = KEY_VALUES_PREFIX + "sources";
401
402        /**
403         * Maximum number of alerts {@link LogAlerts} holds in its ring buffer. Read once,
404         * from whatever {@link LogProperties} {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} has already
405         * resolved by the time it constructs {@link LogAlerts} - before any
406         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} runs.
407         * <p>
408         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.capacity}</code>
409         * @see LogAlerts#DEFAULT_CAPACITY
410         */
411        static final String ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.capacity";
412
413        /**
414         * What {@link LogAlerts} does, once on {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig) start},
415         * if it has recorded at least one error alert and still has zero
416         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener}s registered - see
417         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction} for the three choices and
418         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction#DUMP} for the default.
419         * <p>
420         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.unobservedErrorsAction}</code>
421         */
422        static final String ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unobservedErrorsAction";
423
424        /**
425         * Alert level at which starting Rainbow Gum fails, like treating compiler warnings as
426         * errors: see {@link LogAlerts.FailLevel}. Unlike
427         * {@value #ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} it fails whether or not a
428         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener} is registered.
429         * <p>
430         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.fail}</code>
431         */
432        static final String ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.fail";
433
434        /**
435         * Alert level for property keys that were set but not read while starting: see
436         * {@link LogAlerts.UnusedKeyLevel}.
437         * <p>
438         * Property: <code>{@index logging.alerts.unusedKey}</code>
439         */
440        static final String ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unusedKey";
441
442        /**
443         * Per logger change properties prefix: see {@link ChangeType}.
444         * <p>
445         * Property: <code>{@index logging.change.logger.{logger}}</code>
446         */
447        static final String CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.logger";
448
449        /**
450         * Per logger caller info properties prefix: see {@link LogEvent.Caller.CallerType}.
451         * Independent of {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and {@link #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY}:
452         * resolved through its own logger-name hierarchy walk, so a value here is never
453         * overridden by a more specific {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} entry or vice versa.
454         * <p>
455         * Property: <code>{@index logging.caller.logger.{logger}}</code>
456         */
457        static final String CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "caller.logger";
458
459        /**
460         * Logging file property for default single file appending. The value is a URI or a
461         * file path, including a Windows path such as <code>C:\logs\app.log</code>.
462         * <p>
463         * Property: <code>{@index logging.file.name}</code>
464         */
465        static final String FILE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "file.name";
466
467        /**
468         * A common key parameter is called name.
469         */
470        static final String NAME = "name";
471
472        /**
473         * For properties keys that are parameterized with {@value #NAME} the name often used
474         * if not specified is: {@value #DEFAULT_NAME}.
475         */
476        static final String DEFAULT_NAME = "default";
477
478        /**
479         * Enabled Logging appenders. The value should be a list of names. This is equivalent
480         * to {@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} with name "default".
481         * <p>
482         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appenders}</code>
483         */
484        static final String APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "appenders";
485
486        /**
487         * Logging appender prefix for configuration.
488         */
489        static final String APPENDER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "appender.{" + NAME + "}.";
490
491        /**
492         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's output, followed by the output's
493         * URI scheme, for example <code>logging.appender.{name}.output.file.</code>. Also
494         * used for an output built without an appender.
495         */
496        static final String OUTPUT_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "output.";
497
498        /**
499         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's encoder, followed by the
500         * encoder's URI scheme, for example
501         * <code>logging.appender.{name}.encoder.json5.</code>. Also used for an encoder built
502         * without an appender.
503         */
504        static final String ENCODER_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "encoder.";
505
506        /**
507         * Output appender property.
508         * <p>
509         * Property: <code>{@index logging.appender.{name}.output.uri}</code>
510         */
511        static final String APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY = OUTPUT_PREFIX + "uri";
512
513        /**
514         * Encoder appender property.
515         * <p>

518        static final String APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY = ENCODER_PREFIX + "uri";

541         */

545         * Route prefix for configuration.

562        static final String ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY = PUBLISHER_PREFIX + "uri";

566         * <p>
567         * Property: <code>{@index logging.route.{name}.appenders}</code>

594

596         * Key parameter for the name a {@link LogRouter.Router.Filter filter} is selected
597         * with in {@value #ROUTE_FILTERS_PROPERTY}.
598         */

602         * Prefix of the properties configuring a route's filter, for example
603         * <code>logging.route.default.filter.throttle.rate</code>.

607        /**
608         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String)}.
609         * @param key property name.
610         * @return property value.
611         */
612        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key);
613
614        /**
615         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String, String)} with the exception that the
616         * fallback cannot be null and the return cannot be null.
617         * @param key property name.
618         * @param fallback returned if the value is not found and may not be null.
619         * @return value found or fallback.
620         */
621        default String value(String key, String fallback) {
622                Objects.requireNonNull(fallback);
623                String v = valueOrNull(key);
624                if (v != null) {
625                        return v;
626                }
627                return fallback;
628        }
629
630        /**
631         * Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses
632         * {@link #parseList(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
633         * as a list using {@link LogProperties#parseList(String)} but custom implementations
634         * may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing
635         * configuration system.
636         * <p>
637         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
638         * and percent-encoded (<a href=
639         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
640         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
641         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
642         * logging.appenders=console,file
643         * </code></pre> resolves to <code>["console", "file"]</code>, and: <pre><code>
644         * logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
645         * </code></pre> (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to
646         * <code>["one two", "three,four"]</code>. See {@link #parseList(String)} for empty
647         * elements.
648         * @param key property name.
649         * @return list or <code>null</code>.
650         * @apiNote the reason empty list is not returned for missing key is that it creates
651         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
652         */
653        default @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
654                String s = valueOrNull(key);
655                if (s == null) {
656                        return null;
657                }
658                return parseList(s);
659        }
660
661        /**
662         * Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses
663         * {@link #parseMap(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
664         * as map using {@link LogProperties#parseMap(String)} but custom implementations may
665         * rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration
666         * system.
667         * <p>
668         * The returned map must iterate in a stable order, the same every time for the same
669         * configuration, preferably the order its entries were declared.
670         * <p>
671         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
672         * <code>key=value</code> pairs, percent-encoded (<a href=
673         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
674         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
675         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
676         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
677         * </code></pre> resolves to
678         * <code>{"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}</code>, and: <pre><code>
679         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
680         * </code></pre> (a percent-encoded space) resolves to
681         * <code>{"region": "us east"}</code>.
682         * <p>
683         * When that property is not set, the map can instead be given as a list of its keys
684         * in <code>key.keys</code> and each value in <code>key.</code><em>mapKey</em>, which
685         * works with sources that only hold flat values such as system properties or
686         * environment variables, keeps the declared order, and needs no encoding: <pre><code>
687         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.keys=environment,region
688         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.environment=prod
689         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.region=us east
690         * </code></pre> A key listed without a value is an error.
691         * @param key property name.
692         * @return map or <code>null</code>.
693         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if a key listed in <code>key.keys</code> is empty
694         * or has no value.
695         * @apiNote the reason empty map is not returned for missing key is that it creates
696         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
697         */
698        default @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
699                String s = valueOrNull(key);
700                if (s == null) {
701                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
702                }
703                return parseMap(s);
704        }
705
706        /**
707         * Suffix of the property listing a map's keys, see {@link #mapOrNull(String)}.
708         */
709        static final String MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX = "keys";
710
711        /**
712         * Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and
713         * key directly. A composite/aggregate {@link LogProperties} (one backed by more than
714         * one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in
715         * order, returning the first non-<code>null</code> result - which member actually
716         * produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite
717         * never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a
718         * resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the
719         * first hit.
720         * @param <R> result type.
721         * @param key property key.
722         * @param visitor applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the
723         * visit, key); a <code>null</code> return means keep visiting.
724         * @return first non-<code>null</code> result, or <code>null</code> if nothing visited
725         * produced one.
726         */
727        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
728                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
729                return visitor.apply(this, key);
730        }
731
732        /**
733         * Searches up a {@value #SEP} separated path using this properties to check for
734         * values. The first value not missing (not <code>null</code>) will be returned.
735         * @param <T> result type
736         * @param root prefix.
737         * @param key partial key that will have prefix concated on each try of func.
738         * @param func convert function where <code>null</code> return means to keep
739         * searching.
740         * @return closest value or <code>null</code> if no value can be found.
741         * @see #findUpPathOrNull(String, Function)
742         */
743        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
744        default <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findOrNull(String root, String key,
745                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable T> func) {
746                return findUpPathOrNull(key, k -> func.apply(this, concatKey(root, k)));
747        }
748
749        /**
750         * Starts resolving a property under key against this properties - the preferred entry
751         * point for looking up and converting a property, see {@link LogProperty}.
752         * @param key key, must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with
753         * {@value #SEP}.
754         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
755         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
756         * {@link LogProperty#or(String)}).
757         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if key is malformed.
758         */
759        default LogProperty forKey(String key) {
760                return LogProperty.of(this, key);
761        }
762
763        /**
764         * Starts resolving a property under key, with a <code>{name}</code> placeholder in
765         * key interpolated to nameParam, against this properties.
766         * @param key key, containing a <code>{name}</code> placeholder, and once interpolated
767         * must start with {@value #ROOT_PREFIX} and not start or end with {@value #SEP}.
768         * @param nameParam value to interpolate for <code>{name}</code> in key.
769         * @return a LogProperty ready to be resolved (e.g. via
770         * {@link LogProperty#ofString()}) or given fallback keys to try (via
771         * {@link LogProperty#or(String, String)}).
772         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the interpolated key is malformed.
773         */
774        default LogProperty forKey(String key, String nameParam) {
775                return LogProperty.of(this, key, nameParam);
776        }
777
778        /**
779         * Describes a key and by default is usually just the key.
780         * @param key key.
781         * @return usually the key.
782         */
783        default String description(String key) {
784                return key;
785        }
786
787        /**
788         * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A higher
789         * number gives higher precedence.
790         * @return zero by default.
791         */
792        default int order() {
793                return 0;
794        }

796        /**
797         * Abstract log properties builder.
798         *
799         * @param <T> builder.
800         * @apiNote this abstract class can largely be ignored hence why it is sealed.
801         */
802        public sealed abstract class AbstractBuilder<T> {
803
804                /**
805                 * description
806                 */
807                protected @Nullable String description = null;
808
809                /**
810                 * order
811                 */
812                protected int order = 0;
813
814                /**
815                 * rename key
816                 */
817                protected Function<String, String> renameKey = s -> s;
818
819                /**
820                 * fallbacks
821                 */
822                protected List<LogProperties> fallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
823
824                /**
825                 * Ignored.
826                 */
827                protected AbstractBuilder() {
828                }
829
830                /**
831                 * Add a fallback properties.
832                 * @param properties fallback not null.
833                 * @return this.
834                 */
835                public T with(LogProperties properties) {
836                        this.fallbacks.add(properties);
837                        return self();
838                }
839
840                /**
841                 * For returning this.
842                 * @return this builder.
843                 */
844                protected abstract T self();
845
846                /**
847                 * Description for properties.
848                 * @param description not null.
849                 * @return this.
850                 */
851                public T description(String description) {
852                        this.description = description;
853                        return self();
854                }
855
856                /**
857                 * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A
858                 * higher number gives higher precedence.
859                 * @param order order.
860                 * @return this.
861                 */
862                public T order(int order) {
863                        this.order = order;
864                        return self();
865                }
866
867                /**
868                 * Renames the key before it accesses function.
869                 * @param renameKey rename key function.
870                 * @return this.
871                 */
872                public T renameKey(Function<String, String> renameKey) {
873                        this.renameKey = renameKey;
874                        return self();
875                }
876
877                /**
878                 * Removes the prefix from a key before it accesses the underlying properties.
879                 * @param prefix to be removed from start of key.
880                 * @return this.
881                 */
882                public T removeKeyPrefix(String prefix) {
883                        return renameKey(k -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(k, prefix));
884                }
885
886        }

888        /**
889         * Builder for properties.
890         */
891        public final static class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
892
893                private @Nullable Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider = null;
894
895                private Builder() {
896                }
897
898                @Override
899                protected Builder self() {
900                        return this;
901                }
902
903                private Builder provider(Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider) {
904                        if (this.provider != null) {
905                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("from already set");
906                        }
907                        this.provider = provider;
908                        return this;
909                }
910
911                /**
912                 * Sets what is called on {@link LogProperties#valueOrNull(String)}.
913                 * @param function valueOrNull func.
914                 * @return this.
915                 */
916                public Builder fromFunction(@SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, @Nullable String> function) {
917                        return provider((b) -> new DefaultLogProperties(function,
918                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "function"), renameKey, order));
919                }
920
921                /**
922                 * Parses a string as {@link Properties}.
923                 * <p>
924                 * The parameter is the <strong>contents</strong> of a properties file, not a
925                 * resource, path, or file name. Passing a name such as
926                 * {@code "logging.properties"} does not load that file; it is parsed as a single
927                 * key with an empty value.
928                 * @param properties properties content as a string, for example
929                 * {@code "logging.level=INFO"}.
930                 * @return this.
931                 * @apiNote Rainbow Gum core does not read resources from the filesystem or the
932                 * classpath. If external properties are needed, it is the caller's responsibility
933                 * to read them into a string (or use a module that does, like
934                 * {@code rainbowgum-simple-props}).
935                 */
936                public Builder fromProperties(String properties) {
937                        if (description == null) {
938                                description = "PROPERTIES_STRING";
939                        }
940                        return fromFunction(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties)::get);
941                }
942
943                /**
944                 * Parses a string as a URI query string. If the URI has no query portion then it
945                 * will be equivalent to empty properties.
946                 * @param uri percent encoded uri with separator as "<code>&amp;</code>" and key
947                 * value separator of "<code>=</code>".
948                 * @return this.
949                 */
950                public Builder fromURIQuery(URI uri) {
951                        String query = uri.getRawQuery();
952                        return provider((b) -> queryToProperties(query,
953                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "URI_QUERY(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")")));
954                }
955
956                private MultiMapProperties queryToProperties(@Nullable String query, String description) {
957                        Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
958                        if (query == null) {
959                                multiMap = Map.of();
960                        }
961                        else {
962                                multiMap = parseMultiMap(query);
963                        }
964                        var properties = new MultiMapProperties(multiMap, description, renameKey, order);
965                        return properties;
966                }
967
968                /**
969                 * Builds LogProperties based on builder config.
970                 * @return this.
971                 */
972                public LogProperties build() {
973                        var f = this.provider;
974                        if (f == null) {
975                                if (!fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
976                                        return LogProperties.of(fallbacks);
977                                }
978                                throw new IllegalStateException("from was not set");
979                        }
980
981                        var first = f.apply(this);
982                        if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
983                                return first;
984                        }
985                        List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
986                        combined.add(first);
987                        combined.addAll(fallbacks);
988                        return LogProperties.of(combined);
989                }
990
991                static abstract class AbstractLogProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
992
993                        protected final String description;
994
995                        protected final Function<String, String> renameKey;
996
997                        protected final int order;
998
999                        public AbstractLogProperties(String description, Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1000                                super();
1001                                this.description = description;
1002                                this.renameKey = renameKey;
1003                                this.order = order;
1004                        }
1005
1006                        @Override
1007                        public int order() {
1008                                return this.order;
1009                        }
1010
1011                        @Override
1012                        public String description(String key) {
1013                                String rename = renameKey.apply(key);
1014                                return descriptionForKey(description, rename);
1015                        }
1016
1017                        @Override
1018                        public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1019                                out.append(description);
1020                        }
1021
1022                        @Override
1023                        public String toString() {
1024                                return getClass().getSimpleName() + "[description='" + description + "', " + "order=" + order + "]";
1025                        }
1026
1027                }

1029                private static final class DefaultLogProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
1030
1031                        private final Function<String, @Nullable String> func;
1032
1033                        DefaultLogProperties(Function<String, @Nullable String> func, String description,
1034                                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1035                                super(description, renameKey, order);
1036                                this.func = func;
1037                        }
1038
1039                        @Override
1040                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {

1044                }

1048        /**
1049         * Properties that can list the keys they hold, so that with
1050         * {@link LogConfig.DebugModeType#HELP} (or {@link LogConfig.DebugModeType#ALL}) keys
1051         * that were set but never read can be reported. A source that renames keys should
1052         * name a key the way it is set in the source in {@link #description(String)}, since
1053         * that is how a suggested key is reported.
1054         */
1055        public interface Listable extends LogProperties {
1056
1057                /**
1058                 * The keys this source holds, as they are read (not renamed).
1059                 * @return keys.

1063        }

1065        /**
1066         * A base for properties read from a tree of nodes, such as a TOML, HOCON or YAML
1067         * document, or a configuration system that holds its settings as a tree. A subclass
1068         * says how to get a named member of a node and a node's value, and this class finds
1069         * the node for a key.
1070         * <p>
1071         * This class is only a way to implement {@link LogProperties}. Code that reads
1072         * properties should depend on {@link LogProperties}, not on this class.
1073         * <p>
1074         * A key is split on {@value LogProperties#SEP} into member names, except that a key
1075         * ending with a logger name, such as <code>logging.level.com.example</code>, ends
1076         * with one member: the logger name, which can contain dots or any other character.
1077         * The logger name is looked up as a single member of the node at the rest of the key
1078         * (<code>logging.level</code>) and, if there is no such member, split on
1079         * {@value LogProperties#SEP} like the rest of the key. The level, route level, change
1080         * and caller properties end with a logger name. For example in TOML:
1081         * {@snippet lang = toml :
1082         * [logging.level]
1083         * root = "warn"
1084         * "com.example" = "debug"
1085         * "com.example.sub" = "error"
1086         * }
1087         * The logger name <code>root</code> is the root logger, so a format that cannot have
1088         * a value at <code>logging.level</code> when it has members can set the root logger's
1089         * level as above.
1090         * <p>
1091         * {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} is called once for each lookup and nodes are not kept
1092         * between lookups, so a source whose tree changes at runtime can return its current
1093         * tree. Such a source should call {@link LogConfig.ChangePublisher#publish()} after a
1094         * change.
1095         * <p>
1096         * Methods added to this class in later versions will have names starting with
1097         * <code>do</code>, so a subclass should not declare methods with that prefix.
1098         *
1099         * @param <N> node type.
1100         */
1101        public static abstract class AbstractNested<N> implements LogProperties {
1102
1103                /**
1104                 * For subclasses.
1105                 */
1106                protected AbstractNested() {
1107                }
1108
1109                /**
1110                 * The top node of the tree, called once for each lookup.
1111                 * @return top node or <code>null</code> if there is none.
1112                 */
1113                protected abstract @Nullable N doRootNodeOrNull();
1114
1115                /**
1116                 * A member of a node.
1117                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or this method.
1118                 * @param name member name, which is not empty and may contain
1119                 * {@value LogProperties#SEP}.
1120                 * @return member or <code>null</code> if the node has no member with that name.
1121                 */
1122                protected abstract @Nullable N doMemberNodeOrNull(N node, String name);
1123
1124                /**
1125                 * The value of a node.
1126                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1127                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1128                 * @return value or <code>null</code> if the node has none, for example a node
1129                 * that only has members.
1130                 */
1131                protected abstract @Nullable String doValueNodeOrNull(N node);
1132
1133                /**
1134                 * The value of a node as a list, for a format that has lists. By default
1135                 * <code>null</code>, so {@link #listOrNull(String)} parses
1136                 * {@link #doValueNodeOrNull(Object)}.
1137                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1138                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1139                 * @return list or <code>null</code> if the node is not a list.
1140                 */
1141                protected @Nullable List<String> doListNodeOrNull(N node) {
1142                        return null;
1143                }
1144
1145                /**
1146                 * The value of a node as a map, for a format that has tables of values. By
1147                 * default <code>null</code>, so {@link #mapOrNull(String)} parses
1148                 * {@link #doValueNodeOrNull(Object)} or reads the map's keys from
1149                 * <code>key.keys</code>.
1150                 * @param node a node returned by {@link #doRootNodeOrNull()} or
1151                 * {@link #doMemberNodeOrNull(Object, String)}.
1152                 * @return map, iterating in a stable order, or <code>null</code> if the node is
1153                 * not a table of values.
1154                 */
1155                protected @Nullable Map<String, String> doMapNodeOrNull(N node) {
1156                        return null;
1157                }
1158
1159                @Override
1160                public final @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1161                        N node = node(key);
1162                        return node == null ? null : doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1163                }
1164
1165                @Override
1166                public final @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1167                        N node = node(key);
1168                        if (node == null) {
1169                                return null;
1170                        }
1171                        var list = doListNodeOrNull(node);
1172                        if (list != null) {
1173                                return list;
1174                        }
1175                        String value = doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1176                        return value == null ? null : LogProperties.parseList(value);
1177                }
1178
1179                @Override
1180                public final @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1181                        N node = node(key);
1182                        if (node != null) {
1183                                var map = doMapNodeOrNull(node);
1184                                if (map != null) {
1185                                        return map;
1186                                }
1187                                String value = doValueNodeOrNull(node);
1188                                if (value != null) {
1189                                        return LogProperties.parseMap(value);
1190                                }
1191                        }
1192                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1193                }
1194
1195                private @Nullable N node(String key) {
1196                        N root = doRootNodeOrNull();
1197                        if (root == null) {
1198                                return null;
1199                        }
1200                        var loggerKey = Loggers.Key.parseOrNull(key);
1201                        if (loggerKey == null) {
1202                                return path(root, key);
1203                        }
1204                        N prefix = path(root, loggerKey.prefix());
1205                        String loggerName = loggerKey.loggerName();
1206                        if (prefix == null || loggerName.isEmpty()) {
1207                                return prefix;
1208                        }
1209                        N member = doMemberNodeOrNull(prefix, loggerName);
1210                        return member != null ? member : path(prefix, loggerName);
1211                }
1212
1213                private @Nullable N path(N node, String path) {
1214                        N n = node;
1215                        int start = 0;
1216                        while (true) {
1217                                int end = path.indexOf(SEP, start);
1218                                String name = end < 0 ? path.substring(start) : path.substring(start, end);
1219                                if (name.isEmpty()) {
1220                                        return null;
1221                                }
1222                                N m = doMemberNodeOrNull(n, name);
1223                                if (m == null || end < 0) {
1224                                        return m;
1225                                }
1226                                n = m;
1227                                start = end + SEP.length();
1228                        }
1229                }
1230
1231        }
1232
1233        /**
1234         * A log properties that can be mutated like a map.
1235         */
1236        public interface MutableLogProperties extends LogProperties {
1237
1238                /**
1239                 * Assigns key to a value.
1240                 * @param key key.
1241                 * @param value value if null will remove the key.
1242                 * @return this.
1243                 */
1244                MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value);
1245
1246                /**
1247                 * Builder for MutableLogProperties.
1248                 * @return builder.
1249                 */
1250                public static Builder builder() {
1251                        return new Builder();
1252                }
1253
1254                /**
1255                 * Mutable Log properties builder.
1256                 */
1257                public final class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
1258
1259                        private Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1260
1261                        private Builder() {
1262                        }
1263
1264                        @Override
1265                        protected Builder self() {
1266                                return this;
1267                        }
1268
1269                        /**
1270                         * Sets the backing mutable map.
1271                         * @param map backing map.
1272                         * @return this.
1273                         */
1274                        public Builder with(Map<String, String> map) {
1275                                this.map = map;
1276                                return this;
1277                        }
1278
1279                        /**
1280                         * Parses a string as {@link Properties} useful for unit testing with Java
1281                         * multiline string literal.
1282                         * @param properties properties as a string.
1283                         * @return this.
1284                         */
1285                        public Builder copyProperties(String properties) {
1286                                map.putAll(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties));
1287                                return this;
1288                        }
1289
1290                        /**
1291                         * Builds a mutable log properties.
1292                         * @return mutable log properties.
1293                         */
1294                        public MutableLogProperties build() {
1295                                String description = this.description;
1296                                if (description == null) {
1297                                        description = "custom mutable";
1298                                }
1299                                var first = new MapLogProperties(map, description, renameKey, order);
1300                                if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
1301                                        return first;
1302                                }
1303                                List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
1304                                combined.add(first);
1305                                combined.addAll(fallbacks);
1306                                return new CompositeMutableLogProperties(sort(combined));
1307                        }
1308
1309                        private static final class MapLogProperties extends LogProperties.Builder.AbstractLogProperties
1310                                        implements MutableLogProperties {
1311
1312                                private final Map<String, String> map;
1313
1314                                MapLogProperties(Map<String, String> map, String description, Function<String, String> renameKey,
1315                                                int order) {
1316                                        super(description, renameKey, order);
1317                                        this.map = map;
1318                                }
1319
1320                                @Override
1321                                public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1322                                        return map.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1323                                }
1324
1325                                @Override
1326                                public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
1327                                        Objects.requireNonNull(key);
1328                                        key = renameKey.apply(key);
1329                                        if (value == null) {
1330                                                map.remove(key);
1331                                                return this;
1332                                        }
1333                                        map.put(key, value);
1334                                        return this;
1335                                }
1336
1337                        }
1338
1339                }
1340
1341        }

1343        /**
1344         * LogProperties builder.

1346         */
1347        public static Builder builder() {
1348                return new Builder();

1351        /**
1352         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1353         * use system properties. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and is
1354         * preferred that you get the properties through a config instance instead.</strong>
1355         * @return currently bound properties or system properties.
1356         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1357         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1358         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1359         */
1360        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties() {
1361                return findGlobalProperties(() -> StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
1362        }
1363
1364        /**
1365         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1366         * use the supplier as the fallback. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and
1367         * is preferred that you get the properties through a config instance
1368         * instead.</strong>
1369         * @param fallback supplier to use if no rainbow gum is bound.
1370         * @return currently bound properties or fallback.
1371         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1372         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1373         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1374         */
1375        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties(Supplier<? extends LogProperties> fallback) {
1376                var gum = RainbowGum.getOrNull();
1377                if (gum != null) {
1378                        return gum.config().properties();
1379                }
1380                return Objects.requireNonNull(fallback.get());
1381        }

1383        /**
1384         * Creates log properties from many log properties. Equal properties are only included
1385         * once.
1386         * @param logProperties list of properties.
1387         * @param fallback if the logProperties list is empty.
1388         * @return log properties
1389         */
1390        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties, LogProperties fallback) {
1391                if (logProperties.isEmpty()) {
1392                        return fallback;
1393                }
1394                if (logProperties.size() == 1) {
1395                        return Objects.requireNonNull(logProperties.get(0));
1396                }
1397                var array = sort(logProperties);
1398                return new CompositeLogProperties(array);
1399        }
1400
1401        private static LogProperties[] sort(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1402                @SuppressWarnings("null") // TODO eclipse array issue
1403                LogProperties[] array = logProperties.stream()
1404                        .filter(p -> p != StandardProperties.EMPTY)
1405                        // The same source listed twice adds nothing but noise in reports and errors.
1406                        .distinct()
1407                        .toArray(size -> new LogProperties[size]);
1408                Arrays.sort(array, Comparator.comparingInt(LogProperties::order).reversed());
1409                return array;
1410        }

1413         * Creates log properties from many log properties.

1415         * @return if the logProperties is empty {@link StandardProperties#EMPTY} will be
1416         * used.
1417         */
1418        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1419                return of(logProperties, StandardProperties.EMPTY);
