1422        /**
1423         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1424         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1425         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1426         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1427         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1428         * properties.
1429         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1430         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1431         * parameters.
1432         */
1433        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties) {
1434                return of(uri, prefix, properties, null);
1435        }
1436
1437        /**
1438         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1439         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1440         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1441         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1442         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1443         * properties.
1444         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1445         * @param uriKey where the URI came from.
1446         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1447         * parameters.
1448         */
1449        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties, @Nullable String uriKey) {
1450                /*
1451                 * TODO this should be integrated with the whole providers and registries.
1452                 */
1453                String propDesc = uriKey != null ? "[" + uriKey + "]->" : "";
1454                String description = propDesc + "URI(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")";
1455                var uriProperties = LogProperties.builder()
1456                        .description(description)
1457                        .fromURIQuery(uri)
1458                        .renameKey(s -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(s, prefix))
1459                        .build();
1460                var check = UnusedKeyCheck.findOrNull(properties);
1461                if (check != null) {
1462                        check.addUriQuery(uri, prefix, uriProperties);
1463                        /*
1464                         * Map members such as ?headers.x=y are read inside the query layer, so it is
1465                         * recorded like the config's own layers.
1466                         */
1467                        uriProperties = check.wrap(uriProperties);
1468                }
1469                var queryKeys = new LinkedHashSet<String>();
1470                String query = uri.getRawQuery();
1471                if (query != null) {
1472                        parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> queryKeys.add(prefix + k));
1473                }
1474                return LogProperties.of(List.of(properties, new UriQueryProperties(uriProperties, uriKey, queryKeys)));
1475        }
1476
1477        /**
1478         * Parse a {@linkplain URI#getRawQuery() URI query} in <a href=
1479         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1480         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded </a> format useful for parsing properties values
1481         * that have key values embedded in them. <strong>This parser unlike form encoding
1482         * uses <code>%20</code> for space as the data is coming from a URI.</strong>
1483         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1484         * @param consumer accept will be called for each entry and if key (left hand) does
1485         * not have a "<code>=</code>" following it the second parameter on the consumer
1486         * accept will be passed <code>null</code>.
1487         */
1488        public static void parseUriQuery(String query,
1489                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1490                parseUriQuery(query, true, consumer);
1491        }
1492
1493        /**
1494         * Parses a URI query formatted string to a Map.
1495         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1496         * @return decoded key values with last key winning over previous equal keys.
1497         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1498         */
1499        public static Map<String, String> parseMap(String query) {
1500                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1501                parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> {
1502                        if (v != null) {
1503                                m.put(k, v);
1504                        }
1505                });
1506                return m;
1507        }
1508
1509        /**
1510         * Parses a URI query for a multiple value map. The list values of the map maybe empty
1511         * if the query parameter does not have any values associated with it which would be
1512         * the case if there is a parameter (key) with no "<code>=</code>" following it. For
1513         * example the following would have three entries of <code>a,b,c</code> all with empty
1514         * list: <pre>
1515         * <code>
1516         * a&amp;b&amp;c&amp;
1517         * </code> </pre>
1518         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1519         * @return decoded key values with multiple keys grouped together in order found.
1520         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1521         */
1522        public static Map<String, List<String>> parseMultiMap(String query) {
1523                Map<String, List<String>> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1524                BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> f = (k, v) -> {
1525                        List<String> list = Objects.requireNonNull(m.computeIfAbsent(k, _k -> new ArrayList<String>()));
1526                        if (v != null) {
1527                                list.add(v);
1528                        }
1529                };
1530                parseUriQuery(query, f);
1531                return m;
1532        }
1533
1534        /**
1535         * Parses a list of strings from a string that is <a href=
1536         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1537         * percent encoded for escaping (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)</a> where the
1538         * separator can be either "<code>&amp;</code>" or "<code>,</code>".
1539         * <p>
1540         * An example would be using ampersand: <pre><code>
1541         *  "a&amp;b%20B&amp;c" -> ["a","b B","c"]
1542         *  </code> </pre> and comma: <pre><code>
1543         *  "a,b,c" -> ["a","b","c"]
1544         *  </code> </pre>
1545         * <p>
1546         * An element may be empty. One empty element at the start and one at the end are
1547         * dropped, so a value assembled from parts that may be missing still works
1548         * (<code>"a,"</code> and <code>",a,"</code> are <code>["a"]</code>), while every
1549         * other empty element is kept: <pre><code>
1550         *  "" -> []
1551         *  ",," -> [""]
1552         *  "a,,b" -> ["a","","b"]
1553         *  "a,," -> ["a",""]
1554         *  </code> </pre> An equals sign is part of the element: <code>"a=b"</code> is
1555         * <code>["a=b"]</code>.
1556         * @param query the comma or ampersand delimited string.
1557         * @return list of strings
1558         */
1559        public static List<String> parseList(String query) {
1560                List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
1561                int start = 0;
1562                for (int i = 0; i < query.length(); i++) {
1563                        char c = query.charAt(i);
1564                        if (c == ',' || c == '&') {
1565                                list.add(query.substring(start, i));
1566                                start = i + 1;
1567                        }
1568                }
1569                list.add(query.substring(start));
1570                if (list.get(0).isEmpty()) {
1571                        list.remove(0);
1572                }
1573                if (!list.isEmpty() && list.get(list.size() - 1).isEmpty()) {
1574                        list.remove(list.size() - 1);
1575                }
1576                list.replaceAll(e -> PercentCodec.decode(e, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
1577                return list;
1578        }
1579
1580        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1581                parseUriQuery(query, decode, "[&,]", consumer);
1582        }
1583
1584        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, String sep,
1585                        BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1586                /*
1587                 * TODO default java split has issues but is very fast
1588                 */
1589                @SuppressWarnings("StringSplitter")
1590                String[] pairs = query.split(sep);
1591                for (String pair : pairs) {
1592                        int idx = pair.indexOf("=");
1593                        String key;
1594                        String value;
1595                        if (idx == 0) {
1596                                continue;
1597                        }
1598                        else if (idx < 0) {
1599                                key = pair;
1600                                value = null;
1601                        }
1602                        else {
1603                                key = pair.substring(0, idx);
1604                                value = pair.substring(idx + 1);
1605                        }
1606                        if (decode) {
1607                                key = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1608                                if (value != null) {
1609                                        value = PercentCodec.decode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1610                                }
1611
1612                        }
1613                        if (key.isBlank()) {
1614                                continue;
1615                        }
1616                        consumer.accept(key, value);
1617                }
1618        }
1619
1620        /**
1621         * Common static log properties such as System properties ane environment variables.
1622         */
1623        @CaseChanging
1624        enum StandardProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1625
1626                /**
1627                 * Empty properties. The order is <code>-1</code>.
1628                 */
1629                EMPTY {
1630                        @Override
1631                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1632                                return null;
1633                        }
1634
1635                        @Override
1636                        public int order() {
1637                                return -1;
1638                        }
1639                },
1640                /**
1641                 * Uses {@link System#getProperty(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}. The
1642                 * {@link #order()} is <code>400</code> which the same value as MicroProfile
1643                 * config ordinal.
1644                 */
1645                SYSTEM_PROPERTIES {
1646                        @Override
1647                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1648                                return System.getProperty(key);
1649                        }
1650
1651                        @Override
1652                        public int order() {
1653                                return 400;
1654                        }
1655                },
1656                /**
1657                 * Uses {@link System#getenv(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}.The
1658                 * {@link #order()} is <code>300</code> which is the same value as MicroProfile
1659                 * config ordinal.
1660                 */
1661                ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES {
1662                        @Override
1663                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1664                                return System.getenv(translateKey(key));
1665                        }
1666
1667                        @Override
1668                        protected String translateKey(String key) {
1669                                return key.replace(".", "_");
1670                        }
1671
1672                        @Override
1673                        public int order() {
1674                                return 300;
1675                        }
1676                };
1677
1678                @Override
1679                public String description(String key) {
1680                        String k = translateKey(key);
1681                        return name() + "[" + k + "]";
1682                }
1683
1684                /*
1685                 * Each constant's own per-constant class body (see EMPTY/SYSTEM_PROPERTIES/
1686                 * ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES above) makes getClass() an anonymous subclass with no
1687                 * canonical name, so without this LogPropertiesReporting's fallback chain would
1688                 * land on the description(dummyKey) branch instead: name() alone is a cleaner
1689                 * report for the single most common LogProperties in practice (the default when
1690                 * nothing else is configured).
1691                 */
1692                @Override
1693                public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1694                        out.append(name());
1695                }
1696
1697                /**
1698                 * Translate the key.
1699                 * @param key input
1700                 * @return output
1701                 */
1702                protected String translateKey(String key) {
1703                        return key;
1704                }
1705
1706        }
1707
1708        /**
1709         * Searches a {@value LogProperties#SEP} separated property path recursing up the path
1710         * till a non null value (not missing) is found.
1711         * <p>
1712         * For example assume we have a single property set like
1713         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff=DEBUG</code> and we call this function with
1714         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code>.
1715         * <ol>
1716         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1717         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1718         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff</code> will resolve to <code>"DEBUG"</code>, stop
1719         * and return <code>"DEBUG"</code>.</li>
1720         * </ol>
1721         * @param <T> type to return.
1722         * @param key the initial path.
1723         * @param resolveFunc function that returns the value at path or <code>null</code>.
1724         * @return value or <code>null</code> if no non null value can be found.
1725         */
1726        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
1727        public static <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findUpPathOrNull(String key,
1728                        Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc) {
1729                return searchPath(key, resolveFunc, SEP);
1730        }
1731
1732        private static <T> @Nullable T searchPath(String key, Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc, String sep) {
1733                String tempName = key;
1734                @Nullable T level = null;
1735                int indexOfLastDot = tempName.length();
1736                while ((level == null) && (indexOfLastDot > -1)) {
1737                        tempName = tempName.substring(0, indexOfLastDot);
1738                        level = resolveFunc.apply(tempName);
1739                        indexOfLastDot = tempName.lastIndexOf(sep);
1740                }
1741                if (level != null) {
1742                        return level;
1743                }
1744                return resolveFunc.apply("");
1745        }
1746
1747        /**
1748         * Concats a key using {@link #SEP} to the root prefix.
1749         * @param name key.
1750         * @return concat key.
1751         */
1752        static String concatKey(String name) {
1753                return concatKey(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX, name);
1754        }
1755
1756        /**
1757         * Concats a keys using {@link #SEP} as the separator.
1758         * @param prefix start of key.
1759         * @param name second part of key.
1760         * @return key.
1761         */
1762        static String concatKey(String prefix, String name) {
1763                if (name.equals("")) {
1764                        return prefix;
1765                }
1766                if (prefix.equals("")) {
1767                        return name;
1768                }
1769                if (prefix.endsWith(".")) {
1770                        prefix = prefix.substring(0, prefix.length() - 1);
1771                }
1772                if (name.startsWith(SEP)) {
1773                        return prefix + name;
1774                }
1775                return prefix + SEP + name;
1776        }
1777
1778        /**
1779         * Replace "{name}" tokens in property names.
1780         * @param key property name.
1781         * @param parameters tokens to replace with entry values.
1782         * @return interpolated property key.
1783         * @see #interpolateKey(String, Function)
1784         */
1785        static String interpolateKey(String key, Map<String, String> parameters) {
1786                return interpolateKey(key, parameters::get);
1787        }
1788
1789        /**
1790         * Replaces property <strong>key</strong> parameters by using the lookup function.
1791         * Property keys are often parameterized usually by some name. The parameters are
1792         * surrounded by curly braces and replaced by the lookup function. An example of the
1793         * format is <code>a.{PARAM}</code> which has a parameter named <code>PARAM</code>. If
1794         * the lookup function has <code>PARAM->b</code> then the result will be
1795         * <code>a.b</code>. If a value for a parameter is null (indicates not found) an
1796         * exception is thrown.
1797         * @param key to be interpolated.
1798         * @param lookup function that may return null for a parameter.
1799         * @return interpolated key with all parameters replaced.
1800         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the lookup function does not have a value for a
1801         * parameter.
1802         */
1803        public static String interpolateKey(String key,
1804                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, ? extends @Nullable String> lookup)
1805                        throws IllegalArgumentException {
1806                var parameters = keyParameters(key);
1807                String result = key;
1808                for (String k : parameters) {
1809                        var v = lookup.apply(k);
1810                        if (v == null) {
1811                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
1812                                                "Keyed parameter missing. key: '" + key + "' parameter: '" + k + "'");
1813                        }
1814                        LogProperty.Validator.validateKeyParameterValue(key, k, v);
1815                        result = result.replace("{" + k + "}", v);
1816                }
1817                return result;
1818        }
1819
1820        /**
1821         * Interpolates a named key which is a property key that has a {@value #NAME}.
1822         * @param key with name parameters.
1823         * @param name replace name token.
1824         * @return interpolated property key.
1825         */
1826        static String interpolateNamedKey(String key, String name) {
1827                return interpolateKey(key, Map.of(NAME, name));
1828        }
1829
1830        /**
1831         * Remove key prefix from the key. Prefix should end in "." but this method does not
1832         * check that.
1833         * @param key key whose prefix will be removed.
1834         * @param prefix property name prefix.
1835         * @return prefix removed if the string is prefixed.
1836         */
1837        static String removeKeyPrefix(String key, String prefix) {
1838                if (key.startsWith(prefix)) {
1839                        return key.substring(prefix.length());
1840                }
1841                return key;
1842        }
1843
1844        /**
1845         * Property prefix parameter pattern.
1846         */
1847        static final Pattern PARAMETER_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("\\{(.*?)\\}");
1848
1849        /**
1850         * Extract key parameters with {@link #PARAMETER_PATTERN}.
1851         * @param key also known as property name.
1852         * @return parameters in key.
1853         */
1854        static Set<String> keyParameters(String key) {
1855                Set<String> tokens = new LinkedHashSet<>();
1856                Matcher matcher = PARAMETER_PATTERN.matcher(key);
1857                while (matcher.find()) {
1858                        var t = matcher.group(1);
1859                        if (t == null) {
1860                                throw new IllegalStateException("bug with parameter pattern regex.");
1861                        }
1862                        tokens.add(t);
1863                }
1864                return tokens;
1865        }
1866
1867        /**
1868         * Validate key parameters.
1869         * @param key key to be interpolated with parameters.
1870         * @param parameters names of parameters which must <strong>equal</strong> the set of
1871         * the found parameters. while the order obviously does not matter the set cannot have
1872         * more parameters than found in the key.
1873         */
1874        static void validateKeyParameters(String key, Set<String> parameters) {
1875                var keyParameters = keyParameters(key);
1876                if (!parameters.equals(keyParameters)) {
1877                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Keyed parameter mismatch. key: '" + key + "' , key parameters: "
1878                                        + keyParameters + " provided parameters: " + parameters);
1879                }
1880        }
1881
1882        /**
1883         * Standard way to produce description for a key.
1884         * @param type the properties type name.
1885         * @param key the properties key translated.
1886         * @return description for key.
1887         */
1888        static String descriptionForKey(String type, String key) {
1889                return type + "[" + key + "]";
1890        }
1891
1892        /**
1893         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1894         * similar), without a line number.
1895         * @param type the properties type name.
1896         * @param resource file like name.
1897         * @param key the properties key translated.
1898         * @return description for key.
1899         */
1900        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key) {
1901                return type + "[" + resource + "][" + key + "]";
1902        }
1903
1904        /**
1905         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1906         * similar) at a known index, usually a line number.
1907         * @param type the properties type name.
1908         * @param resource file like name.
1909         * @param key the properties key translated.
1910         * @param index usually line number of where key found.
1911         * @return description for key.
1912         */
1913        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key, long index) {
1914                return type + "[" + resource + ":" + index + "][" + key + "]";
1915        }
1916
1917}

1919final class MultiMapProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
1920
1921        private final Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
1922
1923        public MultiMapProperties(Map<String, List<String>> multiMap, String description,
1924                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1925                super(description, renameKey, order);
1926                this.multiMap = multiMap;
1927        }
1928
1929        @Override
1930        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1931                return _valueOrNull(renameKey.apply(key));
1932        }
1933
1934        private @Nullable String _valueOrNull(String key) {
1935                var list = multiMap.get(key);
1936                if (list == null || list.isEmpty()) {
1937                        return null;
1938                }
1939                return list.get(0);
1940        }
1941
1942        @Override
1943        public @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1944                return multiMap.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1945        }
1946
1947        @Override
1948        public @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1949                String s = valueOrNull(key);
1950                if (s != null) {
1951                        return LogProperties.parseMap(s);
1952                }
1953                var map = PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1954                if (map != null) {
1955                        return map;
1956                }
1957                /*
1958                 * Now we check for dotted notation since key was not set. key.subkey=value
1959                 */
1960                String prefix = renameKey.apply(key) + LogProperties.SEP;
1961                LinkedHashMap<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1962                for (var k : multiMap.keySet()) {
1963                        if (k.startsWith(prefix) && !k.equals(prefix)) {
1964                                String v = _valueOrNull(k);
1965                                if (v != null) {
1966                                        String _k = k.substring(prefix.length());
1967                                        m.put(_k, v);
1968                                }
1969                        }
1970                }
1971                return m.isEmpty() ? null : m;
1972        }
1973
1974}
1975
1976interface ListLogProperties extends LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1977
1978        @Override
1979        default @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1980                for (var props : properties()) {
1981                        var value = props.valueOrNull(key);
1982                        if (value != null) {
1983                                return value;
1984                        }
1985                }
1986                return null;
1987        }
1988
1989        @Override
1990        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
1991                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
1992                for (var props : properties()) {
1993                        var value = props.visit(key, visitor);
1994                        if (value != null) {
1995                                return value;
1996                        }
1997                }
1998                return null;
1999        }
2000
2001        @Override
2002        default String description(String key) {
2003                var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
2004                visit(key, (source, sourceKey) -> {
2005                        descriptions.add(source.description(sourceKey));
2006                        return null;
2007                });
2008                String description = String.join(", ", descriptions);
2009                if (description.length() > 120) {
2010                        return "\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
2011                }
2012                return description;
2013        }
2014
2015        LogProperties[] properties();
2016
2017        default StringBuilder toString(StringBuilder sb) {
2018                sb.append(getClass().getSimpleName());
2019                sb.append("[properties=").append(Arrays.deepToString(properties())).append("]");
2020                return sb;
2021        }
2022
2023        /*
2024         * Reports components separated by commas without the error description's line
2025         * wrapping (via LogPropertiesReporting.describe, the same fallback chain
2026         * LogReporter#appendGlobalProperties uses for the top level LogProperties a LogConfig
2027         * was built with) rather than per key.
2028         */
2029        @Override
2030        default void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
2031                boolean first = true;
2032                for (var p : properties()) {
2033                        if (first) {
2034                                first = false;
2035                        }
2036                        else {
2037                                out.append(", ");
2038                        }
2039                        LogPropertiesReporting.describe(out, p);
2040                }
2041        }
2042
2043}
2044
2045/*
2046 * Shared by ListLogProperties#report(Appendable) (recursively, per component) and
2047 * LogReporter's own appendGlobalProperties(Appendable, LogProperties) (for the top level
2048 * LogProperties a LogConfig was built with), so there is exactly one fallback chain for
2049 * "how do we describe an arbitrary LogProperties for a report": an explicit
2050 * Reportable#report(...) if implemented, else the concrete class' fully qualified name
2051 * (stable and free: no override needed), else, only for the rare case where the FQCN
2052 * itself is null (e.g. one of StandardProperties' own per constant enum bodies, which are
2053 * anonymous classes under the hood, before it implemented Reportable directly),
2054 * description(key) with a dummy key, since that is the only description() such a
2055 * LogProperties is guaranteed to answer at all.
2056 */
2057final class LogPropertiesReporting {
2058
2059        static final String DESCRIBE_KEY = "logging.reporter.describe";
2060
2061        private LogPropertiesReporting() {
2062        }
2063
2064        static void describe(Appendable out, LogProperties properties) throws IOException {
2065                if (properties instanceof LogReporter.Reportable r) {
2066                        r.report(out);
2067                        return;
2068                }
2069                String fqcn = properties.getClass().getCanonicalName();
2070                if (fqcn != null) {
2071                        out.append(fqcn);
2072                        return;
2073                }
2074                out.append(properties.description(DESCRIBE_KEY));
2075        }
2076
2077}

2079@SuppressWarnings("ArrayRecordComponent") // TODO we did this originall because it was hot
2080                                                                                        // path but not anymore
2081record CompositeMutableLogProperties(LogProperties[] properties) implements ListLogProperties, MutableLogProperties {
2082
2083        @Override
2084        @SuppressWarnings("ReferenceEquality") // identity check to avoid self-recursion if a
2085                                                                                        // composite contains itself
2086        public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
2087                for (var p : properties()) {
2088                        if (p instanceof MutableLogProperties mp && mp != this) {
2089                                mp.put(key, value);
2090                                return this;
2091                        }
2092                }
2093                return this;
2094        }
2095
2096        @Override
2097        public String toString() {
2098                return toString(new StringBuilder()).toString();
2099        }
2100
2101}

2112final class PropertiesParser {
2113
2114        private PropertiesParser() {
2115        }
2116
2117        static Map<String, String> readProperties(String input) {
2118                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
2119                StringReader sr = new StringReader(input);
2120                try {
2121                        readProperties(sr, m::put);
2122                }
2123                catch (IOException e) {
2124                        throw new UncheckedIOException(e);
2125                }
2126                return m;
2127        }
2128
2129        static void readProperties(Reader reader, BiConsumer<String, String> consumer) throws IOException {
2130                Properties bp = prepareProperties(consumer);
2131                bp.load(reader);
2132        }
2133
2134        private static Properties prepareProperties(BiConsumer<String, String> consumer) {
2135                // Hack to use properties class to load but our map for preserved order
2136                @SuppressWarnings({ "serial", "nullness" })
2137                Properties bp = new Properties() {
2138                        @Override
2139                        @SuppressWarnings({ "nullness", "keyfor", "UnsynchronizedOverridesSynchronized" }) // checker
2140                                                                                                                                                                                                // bug
2141                        public @Nullable Object put(Object key, Object value) {
2142                                Objects.requireNonNull(key);
2143                                Objects.requireNonNull(value);
2144                                consumer.accept((String) key, (String) value);
2145                                return null;
2146                        }
2147                };
2148                return bp;
2149        }
2150
2151}
2152
2153/*
2154 * The key.keys form of LogProperties.mapOrNull, shared with implementations that override
2155 * it.
2156 */
2157final class PropertyMaps {
2158
2159        private PropertyMaps() {
2160        }
2161
2162        static @Nullable Map<String, String> fromKeys(LogProperties properties, String key) {
2163                String keysKey = key + LogProperties.SEP + LogProperties.MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX;
2164                List<String> keys = properties.listOrNull(keysKey);
2165                if (keys == null) {
2166                        return null;
2167                }
2168                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
2169                for (String k : keys) {
2170                        if (k.isEmpty()) {
2171                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("'" + keysKey + "' has an empty map key");
2172                        }
2173                        String valueKey = key + LogProperties.SEP + k;
2174                        String v = properties.valueOrNull(valueKey);
2175                        if (v == null) {
2176                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
2177                                                "map key '" + k + "' is listed in '" + keysKey + "' but '" + valueKey + "' is missing");
2178                        }
2179                        m.put(k, v);
2180                }
2181                return m;
2182        }
2183
2184}

2186/*
2187 * Marks the layer that holds a component URI's query parameters, so a sensitive property
2188 * can refuse a value from it.
2189 */
2190final class UriQueryProperties extends ForwardingLogProperties {
2191
2192        private final LogProperties delegate;
2193
2194        private final @Nullable String uriKey;
2195
2196        private final Set<String> keys;
2197
2198        UriQueryProperties(LogProperties delegate, @Nullable String uriKey, Set<String> keys) {
2199                this.delegate = delegate;
2200                this.uriKey = uriKey;
2201                this.keys = Set.copyOf(keys);
2202        }
2203
2204        /*
2205         * Whether a query parameter sets the key, including as a map member such as
2206         * ?headers.Authorization=x for headers.
2207         */
2208        boolean sets(String key) {
2209                for (String k : keys) {
2210                        if (k.equals(key) || k.startsWith(key + SEP)) {
2211                                return true;
2212                        }
2213                }
2214                return false;
2215        }
2216
2217        @Override
2218        protected LogProperties delegate() {
2219                return delegate;
2220        }
2221
2222        @Nullable String uriKey() {
2223                return uriKey;
2224        }
2225
2226        @Override
2227        public String toString() {
2228                return delegate.toString();
2229        }
2230
2231}
